sections.content:
You know *según parece* and *podría decirse que* from B2 Unit 21: they hedge, which means they soften a claim. In academic writing a hedge is not shyness. It sets the claim at the strength the evidence allows. Think of a scale. *Los datos demuestran que…* claims certainty, so keep it for conclusive evidence. *Todo parece indicar que…* says the evidence points one way. *Cabe suponer que…* and *cabe pensar que…* say only that the conclusion is reasonable. *Cabe* is impersonal, like *hay*: it has no subject.

You can also limit how far a claim reaches: *en cierta medida* and *hasta cierto punto* (partly), *tender a* (a trend, not a rule), and *no conviene generalizar* (do not stretch the claim beyond your cases).

sections.title: The strength of a claim
rows: Los datos demuestran que el efecto es real.
The data prove that the effect is real. (certain)
Todo parece indicar que el efecto es real.
Everything seems to indicate that the effect is real. (probable)
Cabe suponer que el efecto es real.
It is reasonable to assume that the effect is real. (plausible)
El efecto es real en cierta medida.
The effect is real to some extent. (partial)
Los resultados tienden a mejorar con objetivos claros.
Results tend to improve with clear aims. (a trend)

items.spanish: Cabe pensar que la muestra es demasiado pequeña.
items.english: It is reasonable to think that the sample is too small.

items.spanish: Hasta cierto punto, la tesis se sostiene.
items.english: Up to a point, the thesis holds.

items.spanish: Los datos parecen indicar que el efecto es mayor en los grupos pequeños.
items.english: The data seem to indicate that the effect is greater in small groups.

items.spanish: No conviene generalizar con una muestra tan pequeña; el margen de error es amplio.
items.english: It is not advisable to generalise from such a small sample; the margin of error is wide.

sections.content: One hedge per claim is enough. *Cabe suponer que quizá, en cierta medida…* sounds evasive, and the reader cannot tell what you claim. Put the hedge on the part you are unsure of. English speakers may write *se puede suponer*, which is correct, but *cabe suponer* is the usual written form. After these expressions the verb is in the indicative: *Cabe suponer que el efecto es real*.
